feature1.prompt: The current behavior fails when using SimpleLazyObject with a nested subquery annotation. In the ORM query construction, the output_field property does not correctly handle cases where a lazy object is involved. Instead of properly accessing a specialized attribute, the code always falls back to using the field attribute, which can lead to a TypeError when an integer is expected. The feature should ensure that if a select item has a 'target' attribute, that value is used, thereby restoring the previously valid behavior.
feature1.hint_texts: This feature involves modifying the internal logic of the output_field property. The implementation should introduce a check for a 'target' attribute on the select element in django/db/models/sql/query.py. If present, the target value should be returned; otherwise, the property should fall back to the existing field. Developers should verify that the change covers all standard query use cases and that no regressions arise from other parts of the ORM.
feature1.entrypoint: File: django/db/models/sql/query.py; Method: output_field property (around line 233 in the patch). The focus is on updating the logic so that when self.select has one element, the code returns getattr(select, 'target', None) or select.field.

feature2.prompt: Using SimpleLazyObject with a nested subquery annotation causes a regression that disrupts expected query behavior. The malfunction leads to a TypeError by not accounting for the special nature of lazy objects when they are incorporated in subqueries. The intended improvement is to validate that lazy objects are correctly handled during query construction so that they do not trigger type conversion errors. The system should provide clear evidence that nested subquery annotations work seamlessly when a SimpleLazyObject is used.
feature2.hint_texts: This feature involves expanding the test suite to verify the corrected behavior. Developers should add a new test case that creates a SimpleLazyObject and uses it within a nested subquery annotation, ensuring that the query no longer raises a TypeError. The test should recreate the conditions described in the problem statement and target the scenario that previously failed. In addition, any necessary adjustments to supporting files in the tests directory may be required to accommodate the new test case.
feature2.entrypoint: Files: tests/expressions/tests.py and tests/expressions/models.py. The implementation should include a new test function that verifies the use of SimpleLazyObject in nested subquery annotations and any supporting changes needed in the models if required.
